system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 3 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

A. Draw 1 straight line on this rectangle to divide it into 2 triangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

## Question 2

B. Draw 1 straight line on this rectangle to divide it into 2 rectangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

## Question 3

C. Draw 2 straight lines on this rectangle to divide it into 1 rectangle and 2 triangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

Answer each of the 3 questions.

answer_1.description: Your answer to question 1, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_1.title: Answer 1

answer_2.description: Your answer to question 2, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_2.title: Answer 2

answer_3.description: Your answer to question 3, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_3.title: Answer 3

output.answer_1: Draw one straight diagonal line from the top-left corner of the rectangle to the bottom-right corner. This splits the rectangle into two triangles: an upper-right triangle and a lower-left triangle.
output.answer_2: Draw one straight vertical line from the middle of the top side to the middle of the bottom side. This splits the rectangle into two smaller rectangles of equal size, one on the left and one on the right.
output.answer_3: Draw one horizontal straight line across the full width of the rectangle, partway down, so it meets the left and right sides. This makes a top rectangle and a bottom rectangle. Then, in the bottom rectangle, draw a diagonal from its bottom-left corner to its top-right corner, where the horizontal line meets the right side. The result is 1 rectangle (the top one) and 2 triangles (in the bottom part).
